Yes. The key is to **identify the missed obligation clearly, give the contractual opportunity to cure, and avoid prematurely declaring default or demanding delay damages.**

If you paste **section 11.2 and the contract’s notices clause**, I can check the wording against them. The notices clause matters: sending this to the wrong address or by the wrong method could mean the cure clock never starts.

Here’s a draft based on what you’ve told me, with placeholders to confirm before sending.

---

**FORMAL NOTICE UNDER SECTION 11.2 — FAILURE TO DELIVER PHASE 2**

**Date:** [Date sent]  
**To:** [NexaGrid’s full legal name]  
**Attention:** [Required recipient under the notices clause]  
**Address / email:** [Contractual notice address / email]  
**By:** [Required delivery method]

**Re: [Full agreement name], dated [date], between [your entity’s full legal name] and [NexaGrid’s full legal name] (the “Agreement”)**

Dear [Name]:

[Your entity’s full legal name] gives notice under section 11.2 of the Agreement of the following failure to perform:

Under [section / schedule / milestone reference], NexaGrid was required to deliver [exact contractual description of Phase 2 of the dispatch software] by [contractual due date]. As of the date of this notice, that deliverable has not been received, and the delivery obligation remains outstanding.

NexaGrid is required to cure this failure by delivering [exact outstanding Phase 2 deliverable] in accordance with the Agreement within the thirty-day cure period provided by section 11.2.

Please acknowledge receipt of this notice and confirm the steps NexaGrid will take to complete delivery within that cure period. This request does not extend or otherwise alter the contractual cure period or NexaGrid’s obligations.

If NexaGrid does not cure the identified failure within the applicable cure period, [your entity’s name] reserves its right to declare default and pursue delay damages, in each case to the extent available under, and subject to, the Agreement.

This notice does not itself declare default or demand payment of delay damages. [Your entity’s name] reserves all rights and remedies under the Agreement.

Yours sincerely,  
[Name]  
[Title]  
[Your entity’s full legal name]  
[Contact details]

---

**Before sending:**
- Use the **exact due date and deliverable description**, not “fourteen days ago.” Check for any agreed extensions or changes.
- Follow the notices clause’s **delivery method, recipient, address, and required copies**; keep proof of delivery.
- Check whether the thirty days runs from **sending, receipt, or deemed receipt**, and whether the contract defines how days are counted. Don’t insert a cure deadline until that’s clear.
- If default or damages will be significant, have counsel check the final notice and service requirements before it goes out.
